answer:
Verdict: no

## What happened

PID 654800 (`jobrunner`) exited normally with status 0 at **30,091 ms** into the trace. Its shutdown took **0.1 ms** after the last run of its work threads. The trace continued to **30,604 ms**, so it did not remain alive through the end of the trace.

## What it was doing before exit

Across the trace, it ran a steady loop of **2,997 cycles**, with a median cycle length of **10.000 ms**. The main thread spent **99.6%** of its time in `clock_nanosleep`; the four `job-*` threads were blocked about **99.7–99.8%** of the time, mostly waiting for the main thread to wake them. The process also started **2,998 child processes**, all of which exited normally with status 0.
